text:
maya: Trying to onboard HF model org/special-chat-xt to Redwood Dedicated. Model requires trust_remote_code and defines custom config + chat template. After rw-convert the tokenizer loses system_token and chat outputs start with extra <|system|> repeated.

jon: Which rw-convert flags did you use? Did you pass the trust-remote-code equivalent? rw-convert often sanitizes config.json.

maya: Ran: rw-convert --from hf://org/special-chat-xt --to redwood
No extra flags. rw-convert log shows:

```
INFO: auto_map detected custom config class: SpecialChatConfig
WARN: tokenizer special_tokens_map missing 'system_token'
WARN: sanitized config.json: removed unknown key 'chat_templates'
ERROR: could not import special_chat.configs:SpecialChatConfig, falling back to base AutoConfig
```

sara: That explains it. If auto_map import fails rw-convert uses a base config which doesn't have chat_template handling. The custom tokenizer may set special tokens at runtime (not in config.json), so sanitized config loses them. Two options: vendor tokenizer files (tokenizer.json + special_tokens_map.json) into the repo, or patch config.json to include chat_templates and special_tokens_map before conversion.

ey: also watch the tokenizer class: if it defines `build_inputs_with_special_tokens` behavior, converted tokenizer might not implement it, leading to repeated system tokens in generation.

maya: Repro test locally:

```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('org/special-chat-xt', trust_remote_code=True)
print(tok.special_tokens_map)
# -> {'system_token': '<|system|>', 'pad_token': '<|pad|>'}

# but after rw-convert the redistributable shows:
# {'eos_token': '</s>'}
```

jon: Try cloning the HF repo and running rw-convert pointing at local path so it can import files. Or run rw-convert with `--include-remote-code` / `--trust-remote-code` if available. Also check for auto_map keys like:

```
"auto_map": {"AutoConfig": "special_chat.configs:SpecialChatConfig"}
```

If import fails due to relative imports you may need to adjust PYTHONPATH.

sara: For quantization with bitsandbytes: if tokenizer changed, token IDs shift and quantized model may generate incorrect tokens (extra system token). Always verify token id mapping by comparing `tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|system|>'])` before/after conversion.

maya: Quick fix: patched config.json to include chat_templates and special_tokens_map, re-run rw-convert with local repo path, conversion kept SpecialChatConfig and tokenizer metadata. After that quant tests (4-bit bnb) looked stable.

deploy-bot: Deploy check: model org/special-chat-xt (rev: abc123) converted -> redwood-special-chat-xt, ded 1G GPU pool, smoke tests passed.

ethan: FYI file we added to onboarding checklist: if repo uses trust_remote_code or auto_map, prefer cloning and vendoring tokenizer files + core config keys. Also add a unit-check script that compares special token ids pre/post convert.

maya: thanks, saved me a day. I'll add steps to the model bring-up doc and open a small PR to rw-convert to surface import errors as explicit failures instead of warnings.
